uncited: Application-Specific Reconstructions extend the base 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) optimization framework to handle specialized domains such as human avatars, dynamic bodies, robotics, and plants, which require structural priors or modified training pipelines beyond standard static scene reconstruction.

This family is distinguished from general optimization techniques by its reliance on domain-specific constraints (e.g., mesh embedding, physical priors, or semantic features) to resolve ambiguities inherent in monocular or dynamic inputs, whereas [Base 3DGS Optimization](7549-base-3dgs-optimization.md) focuses on generic photometric loss and densification.

The shared principles of this family are defined by the integration of external domain knowledge into the Gaussian parameter space (position, covariance, opacity, spherical harmonics, or feature fields).

Unlike [Base 3DGS Optimization](7549-base-3dgs-optimization.md), which treats Gaussians as independent entities optimized solely for photometric consistency, application-specific methods impose structural or physical constraints to regularize the solution space.
The application of 3D Gaussian Splatting to specific domains emerged as researchers sought to address the limitations of the base method in handling dynamic, articulated, or semantically rich scenes.
